introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2023. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators are allowed. Formulae booklets are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Two particles A and B are moving on the coordinate axes OX and OY. At time $t$ seconds, particle A is at the point with position vector $\mathbf r=[(1+3t)\mathbf i+2t^2\mathbf j]$ m and particle B is at the point with position vector $\mathbf r=[2t^2\mathbf i-3\mathbf j]$ m. Find

(a) the magnitude of the velocity of particle A relative to particle B when $t=2$. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Velocity is the derivative of position with respect to time.

$$\mathbf v_A=\frac{d\mathbf r_A}{dt}=3\mathbf i+4t\,\mathbf j,\qquad \mathbf v_B=\frac{d\mathbf r_B}{dt}=4t\,\mathbf i.$$

Velocity of A relative to B: $\mathbf v_{A/B}=\mathbf v_A-\mathbf v_B=(3-4t)\mathbf i+4t\,\mathbf j$.

At $t=2$: $\mathbf v_{A/B}=(3-8)\mathbf i+8\mathbf j=-5\mathbf i+8\mathbf j$.

Magnitude: $\sqrt{(-5)^2+8^2}=\sqrt{25+64}=\sqrt{89}\approx9.43$.

**The magnitude is $\sqrt{89}\approx9.43\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) Show that the acceleration of B is constant. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
$\mathbf v_B=4t\,\mathbf i$, so

$$\mathbf a_B=\frac{d\mathbf v_B}{dt}=4\,\mathbf i\ \text{m s}^{-2}.$$

This does not contain $t$: it has fixed magnitude $4\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ and fixed direction (along $\mathbf i$). Hence the acceleration of B is constant. $\blacksquare$

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) Two particles, of masses 2 kg and 3 kg, are moving towards each other with speeds $6\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ respectively. After collision, they coalesce. Find

(a) their common velocity after collision. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Momentum is conserved. Take the direction of motion of the 2 kg particle as positive; the 3 kg particle moves in the opposite direction, so its velocity is $-2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

Before: $2(6)+3(-2)=12-6=6$.

After (coalesced mass $5$ kg, common velocity $v$): $5v$.

$$5v=6\ \Longrightarrow\ v=1.2.$$

**The common velocity is $1.2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, in the original direction of the 2 kg particle.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) the loss in kinetic energy due to the collision. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Kinetic energy before: $\dfrac12(2)(6^2)+\dfrac12(3)(2^2)=36+6=42$ J.

Kinetic energy after: $\dfrac12(5)(1.2^2)=\dfrac12(5)(1.44)=3.6$ J.

Loss $=42-3.6=38.4$ J.

**The loss in kinetic energy is $38.4$ J.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii) Two particles M and N of masses 4 kg and 5 kg are connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The system is released from rest with the strings taut and hanging freely.

(a) Draw a diagram showing all the forces acting on the system. *[1 mark]*
(iii)(b) Find the acceleration of the particles and the tension in the string. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. N (5 kg) moves down and M (4 kg) moves up with acceleration $a$. Apply $F=ma$ to each particle in its direction of motion.

For M (up): $T-4g=4a$ ... (1)

For N (down): $5g-T=5a$ ... (2)

Add (1) and (2): $5g-4g=9a$, so $g=9a$ and

$$a=\frac{10}{9}\approx1.11\ \text{m s}^{-2}.$$

From (1): $T=4g+4a=40+\dfrac{40}{9}=\dfrac{400}{9}\approx44.4$ N.

Check with (2): $5g-T=50-\dfrac{400}9=\dfrac{50}9=5\times\dfrac{10}9$ ✓.

**Acceleration $=\dfrac{10}{9}\approx1.11\ \text{m s}^{-2}$; tension $=\dfrac{400}{9}\approx44.4$ N.**
